QUESTIONS

What people ask before they message.

What does Jwero’s girvi, gold loan & pawn broking software for jewellers do?

Girvi and gold loan software for jewellers: photos and valuation at today’s rate, LTV limits, printed receipts, interest collected automatically, part payments, renewals, release and auctions, all posted to the books. It is part of Jwero One: ₹18,000 a month, every module included, with the first month at ₹3,600.

What is girvi?

Girvi is a loan against pledged gold or silver jewellery, given by a jeweller or pawnbroker. The customer gets the jewellery back when the loan and interest are paid.

Which software is used for girvi?

Girvi or gold loan software records each pledge, works out interest, and tracks renewals, release and auctions. Jwero does this on the same customer record and books as the rest of the jewellery business.

How is girvi interest calculated?

By the scheme on each loan: the rate, simple or compound, and any grace period. Jwero accrues it on schedule, so the amount due on any day is on screen. Try the calculator on this page.

Can interest be collected automatically?

Yes. Interest is collected automatically, with reminders before each due date.

Can I set a maximum loan against the gold’s value?

Yes. Set an LTV limit, and each loan is checked against today’s value of the pledge.

Can customers pay part of the loan?

Yes. Part payments of principal are recorded, and interest is recalculated on the balance.

What happens if a loan is not repaid?

The loan moves through default steps with notices, and the auction and how the proceeds were applied are recorded. Follow your state’s notice rules.

Does it post to the books?

Yes. Every disbursal, interest entry, collection, release and auction posts to the ledger.
